meta.title: IL Adaptive Item Bank
meta.notes: Author-estimated a,b (not online IRT calibration). Socratic feedback never dumps answer letter first on wrong picks. Crypto (btc/evm/xrpl/consensus), math (linalg/prob/opt), and SQL (select/agg) concept tracks added 2026-10-04.

items.stem: Which command lists all files including hidden ones in the current directory?

feedback.A: -a shows entries starting with '.' — hidden files.
feedback.B: -l is long format; it does not imply hidden files.
feedback.C: That changes directory to home; it does not list.
feedback.D: pwd prints the working directory path.

items.stem: An absolute path always starts with…

feedback.A: On Unix, absolute paths begin at the filesystem root '/'.
feedback.B: ./ is relative to the current directory.
feedback.C: ~ expands to home, but absolute paths are not limited to home.
feedback.D: $PATH is an environment variable for executables.

items.stem: What does the shell pipe | do?

choices.text: Sends stdout of left command to stdin of right
Runs both commands on separate hosts

feedback.A: Classic Unix pipeline composition.

items.stem: Mode 755 on a file typically means…

feedback.A: 7=rwx, 5=r-x.
feedback.B: Write for others would need a '2' or '6/7' in that digit.
feedback.D: Setuid is a special bit, not 755.

items.stem: Which tool changes file ownership?

feedback.A: chown changes user/group ownership.
feedback.B: chmod changes mode bits, not owner.
feedback.C: chgrp changes group; chown handles user too.

items.stem: A sticky bit on /tmp mainly prevents…

choices.text: Users deleting others' files in the directory

feedback.A: Sticky on a dir: only owner (or root) may unlink.

items.stem: You want a snapshot of running processes. First tool?

feedback.A: Process table tools are the starting point.
feedback.B: That flushes firewall rules — dangerous and unrelated.

items.stem: systemctl status nginx shows a unit is failed. Next useful step?

choices.text: Disable SELinux permanently as first step

feedback.A: Unit logs usually explain the failure.
feedback.D: Loses transient signal; read logs first.

items.stem: On modern systemd hosts, centralized logs are often in…

feedback.A: systemd-journald stores structured logs.
feedback.C: Git is VCS, not runtime logs.

items.stem: Port 443 is commonly associated with…

feedback.A: TLS-wrapped HTTP typically uses 443.

items.stem: IP addresses are primarily a ___ concern; TCP ports are ___ .

feedback.A: Network vs transport in the common model.
feedback.C: MAC is L2; HTTP is L7.
feedback.D: Physical layer is bits on wire.

items.stem: Usable hosts in a classic /24 (RFC 950 style)?

feedback.A: 2^8 − 2 = 254 usable hosts.

items.stem: Netmask 255.255.255.0 equals…

feedback.A: Twenty-four 1-bits.
Nested prefixes overlap; longest-match wins in routing.
feedback.B: Length alone does not guarantee disjointness.

items.stem: How many addresses in a /28?

feedback.A: 2^(32-28)=16 total addresses.

items.stem: An A record maps…

feedback.A: Classic forward lookup.
feedback.C: Certs are not DNS A records.

items.stem: NXDOMAIN means…

choices.text: The queried name does not exist in DNS

feedback.A: Authoritative negative answer.
feedback.D: Network path, not DNS response code.

items.stem: SNI in TLS helps the server…

choices.text: Choose the right certificate for a hostname

feedback.A: Server Name Indication.

items.stem: HTTP 502 usually indicates…

choices.text: Bad gateway — upstream failure via a proxy

feedback.A: Proxy received invalid upstream response.

items.stem: A Git commit stores…

choices.text: Only a diff with no tree

feedback.A: Content-addressed snapshot model.
feedback.B: Implementation may pack deltas; model is snapshots.

items.stem: A branch in Git is best described as…

choices.text: A movable pointer to a commit
A full copy of all blobs always

feedback.A: Lightweight ref.

items.stem: Detached HEAD — safest way to keep new work?

feedback.A: Name the commit with a branch.

items.stem: Fast-forward merge means…

choices.text: Branch pointer moves forward with no merge commit
Git always invents a merge commit

feedback.A: Linear when no divergence.

items.stem: Interactive rebase is usually wrong when…

choices.text: Rewriting commits already on shared main
Editing a message on your branch

feedback.A: Breaks collaborators' history.

items.stem: Container image layers are…

choices.text: Git commits of the app only

feedback.A: Content-addressed layers.

items.stem: Relying on :latest in production is risky because…

choices.text: The tag can move to a different digest over time

feedback.A: Non-immutable reference.

items.stem: A container's PID 1 should…

choices.text: Always be systemd on the host

feedback.A: Or use a proper init.

items.stem: Compose files mainly help you…

choices.text: Declare multi-container apps for local/dev stacks
Replace Kubernetes in all prod clusters

feedback.A: Services, networks, volumes as code.

items.stem: Pod CrashLoopBackOff — first signal?

feedback.A: Events + previous logs.

items.stem: A Pod is…

choices.text: The smallest deployable unit; one or more containers sharing net/ns

feedback.A: Atomic scheduling unit.

items.stem: A Deployment manages…

feedback.A: Desired replicas + rolling updates.

items.stem: ClusterIP Service selects Pods by…

feedback.A: Service.spec.selector ↔ labels.

items.stem: Liveness probe failing repeatedly typically…

choices.text: Causes kubelet to restart the container

feedback.A: Liveness ≠ readiness.

items.stem: Failing readiness probe means…

choices.text: Pod removed from Service endpoints until ready

feedback.A: Traffic stops; container may keep running.

items.stem: Terraform configuration is primarily written in…

feedback.A: HashiCorp Configuration Language.
feedback.D: May wrap TF, not the language.

items.stem: Terraform state mainly tracks…

choices.text: Mapping of resources to real-world IDs

feedback.A: State is the source of truth for managed objects.

items.stem: terraform plan is used to…

feedback.A: Execution plan / diff.

items.stem: A typical CI pipeline includes…

choices.text: Editing prod DBs by hand first

feedback.A: Feedback before prod.

items.stem: GitHub Actions secrets should be…

choices.text: Stored as encrypted Actions secrets, never in the repo
Committed as plaintext in workflow YAML

feedback.A: Least exposure.

items.stem: on: push in a workflow means…

choices.text: The workflow triggers when commits are pushed

feedback.A: Event-driven CI.

items.stem: GitOps CD emphasizes…

choices.text: Desired state in Git reconciled to the cluster
SSH snowflake edits with no record

feedback.A: Declarative pull-based sync.

items.stem: Least privilege means…

choices.text: Grant only the permissions needed for the task

feedback.A: Core IAM principle.

items.stem: A security group / firewall rule set typically filters…

choices.text: Allowed ingress/egress by port, protocol, source/dest

feedback.A: Network access control.

items.stem: Object storage (S3-like) is best for…

choices.text: Durable blobs addressed by key, not a POSIX disk

feedback.A: Objects ≠ block devices.

items.stem: An SLI is…

choices.text: A quantitative measure of service level (e.g. success rate)

feedback.A: Indicator; SLO is the target.

items.stem: A good page-worthy alert is…

choices.text: Actionable, tied to user impact, not raw noise

feedback.A: Alert hygiene.

items.stem: Runtime secrets should live in…

choices.text: A secrets manager / sealed store — not git

feedback.A: Rotate-able, audited.

items.stem: Scanning container images in CI helps catch…

feedback.A: Shift-left supply chain.

items.stem: Which directory usually holds user home folders on Linux?

feedback.A: User homes typically under /home.

items.stem: Sending SIGTERM to a process typically…

feedback.A: Default kill signal is TERM.

items.stem: Longest prefix match means routers prefer…

feedback.A: Longer prefix wins.

items.stem: git status shows…

choices.text: Working tree / staging vs HEAD differences

feedback.A: Status overview.

items.stem: Rolling update on a Deployment aims to…

choices.text: Replace Pods gradually to keep availability

feedback.A: MaxUnavailable/MaxSurge controls.

items.stem: Failing tests in CI should…

choices.text: Block merge/deploy until fixed or explicitly overridden
Page every engineer for flake noise only

feedback.A: Quality gate.

items.stem: Root / highly privileged accounts should be…

feedback.A: Break-glass pattern.

items.stem: High error-rate SLI breach suggests…

choices.text: Investigate recent deploys, deps, and saturation

feedback.A: Symptom → causes.

items.stem: Pinning image digests improves…

feedback.A: Immutable reference.

items.stem: A Terraform provider is responsible for…

choices.text: Talking to an API (cloud/SaaS) to CRUD resources

feedback.A: Plugin boundary.

items.stem: Bitcoin has no accounts at the protocol level. What is the unit of value a transaction spends?

choices.text: An unspent transaction output (UTXO), identified by txid + output index
An account balance entry in a global state trie
A wallet file on the sender's disk

feedback.A: Correct: value exists only as UTXOs; wallets sum them into a 'balance'.
feedback.B: That is Ethereum's account model, not Bitcoin's.
feedback.C: Wallets are local software; the protocol knows only UTXOs.
feedback.D: Coinbase outputs are one kind of UTXO, not the unit itself.

items.stem: A transaction has inputs totaling 0.5 BTC and outputs totaling 0.499 BTC. What is the miner fee?

choices.text: 0.001 BTC — the fee is implicit: inputs minus outputs
0 BTC — there is no fee field
It is invalid without an explicit fee field

feedback.A: Correct: no fee field exists; miners claim the difference.
feedback.B: No fee field does not mean no fee — the difference is the fee.
feedback.C: Outputs keep their value; only the difference goes to the miner.
feedback.D: The transaction is valid; implicit fees are the design.

items.stem: Which sighash flag lets a signer commit to all outputs while allowing others to add inputs later?

feedback.A: Correct: ANYONECANPAY signs only your input; ALL locks every output.
feedback.B: NONE commits to no outputs at all.
feedback.C: ALL alone commits to the full input set too.
feedback.D: SINGLE commits to the one output at your input's index.

items.stem: A miner wants to spend a coinbase output 50 blocks after mining it. Consensus says:

choices.text: Wait — coinbase outputs mature after 100 confirmations
Spendable after 6 confirmations like any output
Coinbase outputs can never be spent

feedback.A: Correct: the 100-block maturity rule guards against reorged rewards.
feedback.B: No grace period is skipped for the block producer.
feedback.C: 6 confirmations is a wallet convention, not the maturity rule.
feedback.D: Coinbase outputs are spendable once mature.

items.stem: Segregated witness changed how transaction weight is counted. Which statement is true?

choices.text: Witness bytes count at a 1:4 discount toward the 4M weight-unit block limit
Witness data is not stored by full nodes
Segwit removed the block size limit entirely
Legacy and segwit transactions weigh the same

feedback.A: Correct: non-witness bytes count 4, witness bytes count 1.
feedback.B: Full nodes store and validate witness data.
feedback.C: The limit became 4M weight units, not unlimited.
feedback.D: The discount is exactly what makes segwit cheaper per byte.

items.stem: Nodes refuse to relay a 200-sat output. Why?

choices.text: Dust policy: it costs more in fees to spend than it is worth, and every node stores it forever
Outputs must exceed 1000 sats by consensus

feedback.A: Correct: uneconomic outputs bloat the UTXO set all full nodes keep.
feedback.B: The supply cap is unrelated to output size.
feedback.C: Dust is policy/standardness, not a consensus amount rule.
feedback.D: Segwit has no minimum output rule.

items.stem: nLockTime is set to a future height, but an input has nSequence = 0xFFFFFFFF. Effect?

choices.text: Locktime is disabled — max sequence opts out of absolute and relative locktimes
Locktime still applies; sequence only signals RBF
A relative locktime of max blocks applies

feedback.A: Correct: final sequence means 'no timelock conditions'.
feedback.B: It is valid and confirmable immediately.
feedback.C: Sequence governs locktime opt-out, not just RBF.

items.stem: 400 weight units of non-witness data plus 400 weight units of witness data gives:

feedback.B: You must weight non-witness bytes at 4x.
feedback.D: Only if there were no witness discount.

items.stem: A transaction input references a previous output by:

choices.text: Outpoint: the previous txid plus the output index (vout)
The block hash and Merkle proof

feedback.A: Correct: the outpoint uniquely names one UTXO in history.
feedback.B: Inputs never name addresses or amounts directly.
feedback.D: Merkle proofs are for SPV, not input references.

items.stem: Your low-fee transaction did not signal RBF and is stuck. The legitimate fix is:

choices.text: Child-pays-for-parent: confirm it inside a high-fee child transaction package
Double-spend the input with a higher fee
Wait — nothing can ever unstick it

feedback.A: Correct: miners take the package; the child's fee pays for the parent.
feedback.B: That is a double-spend attempt, not a fix.
feedback.C: Rebroadcasting changes nothing about miner incentives.
feedback.D: CPFP exists precisely for this case.

items.stem: The block subsidy halves every:

feedback.A: Correct: the halving interval is block-count based, ~4 years.
feedback.C: It is block height, not wall-clock, that triggers it.

items.stem: withdraw() does msg.sender.call{value:amt}('') BEFORE zeroing the balance. The vulnerability is:

choices.text: Reentrancy — the receiver can re-enter and drain funds before state updates
Integer overflow in the call value
Gas griefing — the call forwards 63/64 of gas

feedback.A: Correct: effects must precede interactions; update state first.
feedback.B: Solidity 0.8 checks arithmetic; this is control flow.
feedback.D: Ordering attacks target DEXs, not this pattern.

items.stem: An admin gate uses require(tx.origin == owner). A user is phished into calling an attacker contract that calls the vault. Result?

choices.text: The check passes for the attacker — tx.origin is the tricked user's EOA
It reverts — tx.origin equals the immediate caller
Contracts cannot call contracts, so nothing happens

feedback.A: Correct: tx.origin is the original signer. Authorize with msg.sender.
feedback.D: This is a full vault-draining primitive.

items.stem: A proxy delegatecalls to an implementation whose storage variable order differs. Risk?

choices.text: Storage collision — callee code runs against the proxy's layout; mismatched ordering corrupts state

feedback.A: Correct: keep upgrade layouts append-only with storage gaps.
feedback.B: No remapping exists; slots are positional.
feedback.C: Gas is not the risk here.
feedback.D: The proxy stays upgradeable — and corruptible.

items.stem: The checks-effects-interactions pattern orders operations as:

choices.text: Validate inputs, update state, then interact with external contracts
Interact first for speed, then update state
Update state only after the full transaction
Effects are optional if gas is limited

feedback.A: Correct: state is settled before untrusted code runs.
feedback.B: External calls first is the reentrancy pattern.
feedback.C: State updates must precede the external call.

items.stem: maxFeePerGas = 100 gwei, maxPriorityFeePerGas = 2 gwei, gasLimit = 21000. Maximum total fee you sign for?

choices.text: 21000 × 100 gwei — the gas limit times the max fee per gas

feedback.A: Correct: worst case is limit × maxFeePerGas.
feedback.B: The tip is bounded by the max too.
feedback.C: Fees scale with gas used, not flat.
feedback.D: You pay base+tip up to your max.

items.stem: token.call(abi.encodeWithSignature('transfer(address,uint256)',to,amt)) ignores the return value. Bug?

choices.text: Silent failure — low-level calls return a bool; a reverted transfer looks successful
No bug — transfer always reverts loudly

feedback.A: Correct: check the return or use a safe wrapper.
feedback.B: The callee is trusted here; the bug is the ignored bool.
feedback.C: Call gas is not the issue.
feedback.D: Low-level calls do not propagate reverts.

items.stem: payout() loops over an unbounded array pushing funds. As it grows:

choices.text: DoS via block gas limit — eventually no block fits the loop; use pull payments
Nothing — gas scales with the array

feedback.A: Correct: unbounded loops hit the block ceiling and lock funds.
feedback.B: Push then update is a different bug.
feedback.C: Slots are positional, not collided here.
feedback.D: Gas has a hard per-block cap.

items.stem: setFee(uint) has no access modifier. Classification and fix?

choices.text: Missing access control — gate with onlyOwner or role-based auth

feedback.A: Correct: anyone could rewrite protocol parameters.
feedback.B: Ordering attacks need a DEX, not a setter.
feedback.C: A timelock without auth still lets anyone queue.

items.stem: A large DEX swap sets amountOutMin = 0 in a public mempool. The MEV risk?

choices.text: Sandwich attack — frontrun the price up, backrun after, user keeps the worst fill

feedback.A: Correct: zero slippage tolerance invites sandwiches; set a real minimum.
feedback.D: Atomicity does not stop ordering games.

items.stem: A lending pool prices collateral from a single DEX spot read in the same transaction. Attack?

choices.text: Flash-loan price manipulation — skew spot, borrow against it, repay; use TWAP/oracle networks
No attack — spot is the true price

feedback.A: Correct: single-block spot is manipulable; time-weight or decentralize.
feedback.D: Spot in one block is attacker-settable.

items.stem: Two uint128 variables declared consecutively in a struct occupy:

choices.text: One 32-byte storage slot — sub-256-bit values pack together
Two slots — each variable gets its own
Half a slot each in transient storage

feedback.A: Correct: contiguous sub-word types pack into one slot.
feedback.C: Packing is a storage-layout rule, not optimizer luck.
feedback.D: The optimizer never changes storage layout.

items.stem: An account has 3 trust lines and 2 open offers. Base reserve 1 XRP, owner reserve 0.2 XRP. Total reserve?

feedback.A: Correct: reserve = base + owner_reserve × OwnerCount.

items.stem: Account sequence is 7; a transaction with sequence 5 arrives. Result?

choices.text: Rejected — the sequence must exactly equal the account's next sequence

feedback.A: Correct: strict sequencing prevents replays and reordering.
feedback.C: The ledger does not queue out-of-order.

items.stem: You receive issued tokens without ever creating a trust line to the issuer. What happens?

choices.text: The payment fails — receipt of issued currency requires an opt-in trust line

feedback.A: Correct: trust lines are explicit opt-in; no line, no receipt.
feedback.B: Unsolicited IOUs are blocked by design.
feedback.D: Issuers are not fined for this.

items.stem: An exchange deposit omits the required destination tag. Likely outcome?

choices.text: Funds land in the pooled wallet unattributed to you — the tag is the account number

feedback.A: Correct: custodians share one address; tags route internally.

items.stem: XRPL ledgers close roughly every:

feedback.A: Correct: XRPL's consensus closes ledgers in seconds.

items.stem: An issuer freezes a trust line. Effect on holders of that issued currency?

choices.text: Those tokens cannot move until unfrozen — freezing is issuer-level control

feedback.A: Correct: freeze halts transfers of that IOU on those lines.
feedback.B: Existing holdings are immobilized, not just issuance.

items.stem: Selling a thinly-traded token for XRP without specifying a path typically:

choices.text: Autobridges through XRP order books, walking the book at worsening prices
Gives the mid price regardless of depth

feedback.A: Correct: offers match in price order; thin books mean slippage.
feedback.B: A direct offer can execute without a path.

items.stem: In XLS-20 NFTs, the taxon field is used to:

choices.text: Group/limit minting — e.g. an issuer can cap editions per taxon

feedback.A: Correct: taxon is the edition-grouping identifier.
feedback.C: No royalty field exists on XLS-20.

items.stem: XLS-30 AMM liquidity providers receive:

choices.text: LP tokens representing their pool share, redeemable for underlying assets

feedback.A: Correct: LP tokens track pro-rata pool ownership.
feedback.B: Yield comes from fees on redemption, not direct XRP.

items.stem: Production key hygiene for a funded XRPL account is:

choices.text: Set a regular key for daily signing and disable the master keypair
Share the master secret with the team

feedback.A: Correct: regular keys limit blast radius; the master stays offline.
feedback.D: An account needs a signing key.

items.stem: In proof-of-work, the canonical chain is the one with:

choices.text: The most accumulated work, not simply the longest header count

feedback.A: Correct: chainwork decides; headers alone can mislead.
feedback.B: Transaction count is irrelevant to validity.

items.stem: Solana's proof-of-history provides:

choices.text: A verifiable, sequential clock embedded in the ledger via chained hashes

feedback.A: Correct: PoH proves time passed between events without consensus.

items.stem: Tendermint BFT needs what fraction of voting power to finalize a block?

choices.text: More than 2/3 prevoting and precommitting in each round

feedback.A: Correct: >2/3 quorum gives both safety and liveness.
feedback.D: 1/3+ is the fault tolerance bound, not the quorum.

items.stem: Cardano's Ouroboros selects slot leaders:

choices.text: By stake-weighted lottery, with the schedule known ahead of the epoch

feedback.A: Correct: stake proportion sets leadership probability.

items.stem: Avalanche's Snow consensus reaches agreement by:

choices.text: Repeated random subsampling: validators poll peers and converge on the majority color

feedback.A: Correct: metastable sampling converges without all-to-all voting.

items.stem: Polkadot's relay chain provides parachains with:

feedback.A: Correct: parachains lease shared validator security.

items.stem: Hedera Hashgraph orders transactions using:

choices.text: Gossip-about-gossip with virtual voting on a DAG of events

feedback.A: Correct: the hashgraph DAG plus virtual voting yields fair ordering.

items.stem: Probabilistic finality (PoW) differs from BFT finality in that:

choices.text: PoW finality deepens with confirmations but is never absolute; BFT finality is explicit at commit
PoW is instant and BFT is slow

feedback.A: Correct: confirmations are statistical confidence; BFT commit is a decision.
feedback.D: PoW reorgs are the reason for confirmations.

items.stem: A 51% attack on a PoW chain lets the attacker:

choices.text: Reorg recent blocks to double-spend, but not mint coins out of thin air or steal others' keys
Take anyone's funds without their keys

feedback.A: Correct: majority hashpower reorders recent history; consensus rules still bind issuance.

items.stem: In Cosmos, IBC enables:

choices.text: Trust-minimized token and data transfer between independent sovereign chains via light-client proofs

feedback.A: Correct: light clients verify counterparty state; relayers ferry packets.

items.stem: A matrix W has shape (3, 4) and x is a vector in R^4. What is the shape of Wx?

choices.text: A vector in R^3 — inner dimensions (4) agree, outer give (3,1)
A vector in R^4 — shapes are preserved

feedback.B: The output lives in the row space dimension.
feedback.C: That is the Hadamard product, not matvec.

items.stem: The identity matrix I satisfies, for any compatible A:

feedback.A: Correct: I is the multiplicative identity.
feedback.B: Only the zero matrix gives zero.

items.stem: For matrices A (m×n) and B (n×p), (AB)^T equals:

choices.text: B^T A^T — transpose reverses the order
AB — transpose is a no-op on products

feedback.A: Correct: reversal is required; check dimensions.
feedback.C: BA may not even be defined.

items.stem: Solving Ax = b by elimination fails with 0 = 1 in a row. This means:

choices.text: b is not in the column space of A — no solution exists
x must be the zero vector

feedback.A: Correct: inconsistency means b is outside the reachable outputs.

items.stem: Av = λv with v ≠ 0 defines:

choices.text: An eigenvector v with eigenvalue λ — A stretches v without rotating it

feedback.A: Correct: the defining equation of eigenpairs.

items.stem: The SVD factors an m×n matrix A as UΣV^T. Σ is:

choices.text: m×n diagonal with nonnegatives (singular values) in descending order
The matrix of eigenvectors of A

feedback.A: Correct: Σ carries the singular values on its diagonal.
feedback.B: Σ matches A's shape, not square unless A is.
feedback.C: U and V are the orthogonal factors.
feedback.D: Eigenvectors of A^TA / AA^T, not A.

items.stem: Rank of a matrix equals:

choices.text: The number of pivots — the dimension of the column (and row) space

feedback.A: Correct: rank is the dimension of the image.

items.stem: The dot product u·v = 0 for nonzero u, v means:

feedback.A: Correct: zero inner product is orthogonality.

items.stem: The Euclidean norm ||x||₂ of x = (3, 4) is:

feedback.A: Correct: sqrt(3² + 4²) = 5.

items.stem: A square matrix is invertible iff:

choices.text: Its determinant is nonzero — equivalently, full rank with trivial nullspace

feedback.A: Correct: det ≠ 0 ⟺ n pivots ⟺ only the trivial solution to Ax=0.

items.stem: Projecting b onto the column space of A solves:

choices.text: The least-squares problem min ||Ax − b||² — the normal equations A^TAx = A^Tb

feedback.A: Correct: the closest point in the column space minimizes residual norm.
feedback.B: Exact solve needs b in the column space.

items.stem: Two independent events each have probability 0.1. P(both occur) is:

feedback.A: Correct: 0.1 × 0.1 = 0.01 for independent events.

items.stem: Bayes' rule P(H|E) equals:

choices.text: P(E|H)P(H) / P(E) — prior times likelihood, normalized

feedback.A: Correct: posterior ∝ likelihood × prior.

items.stem: A fair die's expected value is:

choices.text: Cannot be computed for discrete outcomes

feedback.B: No face shows 3.5; expectation need not be attainable.

items.stem: Variance measures:

choices.text: Spread — the expected squared deviation from the mean

feedback.A: Correct: Var(X) = E[(X−μ)²].

items.stem: P(A|B) = 0.9 while P(A) = 0.01. Learning B occurred should:

choices.text: Massively raise your belief in A — evidence updates priors, it does not replace them

feedback.A: Correct: posterior blends likelihood with the base rate.
feedback.B: Ignoring evidence is the base-rate fallacy in reverse.

items.stem: For any event A, P(not A) equals:

feedback.A: Correct: the complement rule.

items.stem: X ~ Binomial(n=100, p=0.1). E[X] is:

feedback.A: Correct: binomial mean is np.

items.stem: For a normal distribution, about 95% of mass lies within:

feedback.A: Correct: the 68–95–99.7 rule.

items.stem: The law of large numbers says:

choices.text: Sample averages converge to the expected value as n grows

feedback.A: Correct: averages stabilize on the mean.
feedback.B: Normality needs the CLT plus conditions.
feedback.D: Outliers persist; they just average out.

items.stem: Flipping a fair coin 10 times, P(exactly 5 heads) is maximized at p=0.5 because:

choices.text: Maximum likelihood: the observed frequency 5/10 maximizes the likelihood

feedback.A: Correct: MLE for coin bias is the observed frequency.
feedback.B: Fairness is the conclusion, not the premise.
feedback.C: Symmetry helps but MLE is the principle.

items.stem: A test catches 99% of defects and flags 5% of good units. Defects are 1 in 1000. A flagged unit is defective with probability about:

choices.text: 2% — Bayes: rare defects mean most flags are false alarms

feedback.B: Detection rate is P(flag|defect), not P(defect|flag).

items.stem: Gradient descent updates parameters by stepping:

choices.text: Opposite the gradient — the direction of steepest decrease

feedback.A: Correct: −∇L is the locally steepest descent direction.

items.stem: Training loss explodes after a few gradient steps. First fix to try:

choices.text: Reduce the learning rate — the step exceeds the stability limit
Increase the learning rate to escape

feedback.A: Correct: divergence with fixed steps almost always means η too large.
feedback.B: Depth does not fix step size.

items.stem: Backpropagation is an application of:

choices.text: The chain rule — layer-local derivatives multiply into the full gradient
The product rule on the loss alone

feedback.A: Correct: dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx) applied layer by layer.
feedback.B: Products appear via the chain rule.

items.stem: A twice-differentiable function is convex iff its Hessian is:

choices.text: Positive semidefinite everywhere — curvature never turns downward

feedback.A: Correct: PSD Hessian ⟺ convex; then every stationary point is global min.

items.stem: At a saddle point, the Hessian has:

choices.text: Both positive and negative eigenvalues — min in some directions, max in others

feedback.A: Correct: indefinite Hessian is the saddle signature.

items.stem: Lagrange multipliers handle:

choices.text: Equality-constrained optimization — ∇f parallel to ∇g at the optimum

feedback.A: Correct: the constrained optimum aligns the gradients.

items.stem: d/dx (x³) equals:

feedback.A: Correct: power rule.

items.stem: ∂/∂x (x²y + 3x) equals:

feedback.A: Correct: partials treat other variables as constants.

items.stem: Adding an L2 penalty λ||w||² to least squares:

choices.text: Shrinks weights toward zero, damping the noisy small-singular-value directions most

feedback.A: Correct: ridge shrinks via σᵢ/(σᵢ²+λ) per singular direction.

items.stem: Newton's method uses second-order information via:

choices.text: The Hessian — stepping by −H⁻¹∇f for locally quadratic convergence

feedback.A: Correct: curvature-corrected steps converge quadratically near minima.

items.stem: WHERE filters rows ___; HAVING filters ___.

feedback.A: Correct: WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY.
feedback.C: They apply at different pipeline stages.

items.stem: An INNER JOIN returns:

choices.text: Only rows with matches on both sides
All rows from the left table

feedback.A: Correct: inner keeps the intersection.

items.stem: In SQL, NULL = NULL evaluates to:

choices.text: UNKNOWN — use IS NULL, never = NULL

feedback.A: Correct: three-valued logic; equality with NULL is never true.
feedback.C: It is not false, it is unknown.

items.stem: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM users returns:

feedback.A: Correct: DISTINCT dedupes the projected rows.

items.stem: To find names starting with 'A', the WHERE clause is:

feedback.A: Correct: % wildcards the rest; _ would match one char.
feedback.B: That finds names ending in A.

items.stem: Table aliases primarily:

choices.text: Shorten references and disambiguate same-named columns in joins

feedback.A: Correct: aliases are namespace hygiene for multi-table queries.

items.stem: NOT IN with a NULL in the subquery list returns:

choices.text: No rows — every comparison becomes UNKNOWN; use NOT EXISTS

feedback.A: Correct: x NOT IN (…, NULL) is never TRUE.

items.stem: ORDER BY 2 in SELECT a, b means:

choices.text: Sort by the second select-list column

feedback.A: Correct: positional ordering refers to select-list position.
feedback.B: Literals in ORDER BY are positions.

items.stem: A correlated subquery:

choices.text: References the outer query and re-executes per outer row
Runs once before the outer query
Is always faster than a join

feedback.A: Correct: correlation binds inner to outer per row.

items.stem: COUNT(*) vs COUNT(email):

choices.text: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(email) skips NULL emails

feedback.A: Correct: * counts rows; column form ignores NULLs.
feedback.B: NULL emails vanish from the column count.

items.stem: LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20 returns:

feedback.A: Correct: skip 20, take 10 — needs ORDER BY for determinism.

items.stem: Every non-aggregated column in the SELECT list must:

choices.text: Appear in the GROUP BY (or be functionally dependent on it)

feedback.A: Correct: the grouping key defines the grain; the rule enforces it.
feedback.B: Aggregates are the alternative, not the requirement.

items.stem: HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 keeps:

choices.text: Groups with more than 5 rows — HAVING filters after aggregation

feedback.A: Correct: HAVING predicates on group properties.

items.stem: SUM(amount) after joining orders to a 3-items-per-order table returns 3× revenue because:

choices.text: Join fan-out: each order's amount repeats per item row — pre-aggregate before joining

feedback.A: Correct: aggregate at the order grain first, then join.
feedback.B: SUM is correct; the grain is wrong.

items.stem: AVG(score) over rows with some NULL scores:

choices.text: Ignores NULLs — averages only non-NULL values

feedback.A: Correct: aggregates skip NULLs (except COUNT(*)).
feedback.C: One NULL does not null the avg.

items.stem: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) gives:

feedback.A: Correct: dedupes before counting.

items.stem: A window function like ROW_NUMBER() differs from GROUP BY because it:

choices.text: Returns a value per row without collapsing rows

feedback.A: Correct: windows compute across rows while preserving them.
feedback.C: ORDER BY defines the window frame.

items.stem: GROUP BY dept, year produces:

feedback.A: Correct: grouping keys compose into finer grains.
feedback.B: That is GROUP BY dept alone.
feedback.C: That is GROUP BY year alone.

items.stem: In the logical query order, aggregation happens:

choices.text: After WHERE and GROUP BY, before HAVING/SELECT/ORDER BY

feedback.A: Correct: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY.

items.stem: SUM(CASE WHEN status='paid' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) computes:

choices.text: Conditional aggregation — total of paid amounts in one pass

feedback.A: Correct: CASE inside aggregates pivots conditions into measures.

items.stem: MIN(event_time) and MAX(event_time) per user give:

choices.text: Each user's first and last event — session boundaries from one pass

feedback.A: Correct: grouped extrema are the standard sessionization seed.
